subject.title: Bug: messaging tool suppress mechanism skips when tool fails then retries in same turn, causing duplicate delivery

question: Should matching assistant replies be held while a same-route message-tool retry is in flight, then dropped on confirmed delivery and released on failure or unresolved turn end?
rationale: The source proves the duplicate timing gap, but choosing release timing and match granularity changes user-visible fallback behavior and could trade duplicate messages for suppressed replies.

options.title: Hold And Release Same Route
options.body: Hold matching replies for in-flight message-tool sends, drop them only after confirmed delivery, and release by default if the send fails or never resolves before turn end.

options.title: Keep Current Fallback Semantics
options.body: Leave committed-success-only suppression in place until a broader delivery lifecycle design can avoid both duplicates and silent drops.

options.title: Suppress On Pending Send
options.body: Treat pending sends as already delivered, accepting the risk that failed or unresolved sends can leave the user with no visible reply.

recommendation.title: Hold And Release Same Route
recommendation.body: Hold matching replies for in-flight message-tool sends, drop them only after confirmed delivery, and release by default if the send fails or never resolves before turn end.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses embedded message-tool bookkeeping, channel fallback semantics, and current integration history for this delivery surface.
